articles.headline: Broncos OC Davis Webb says 'not ideal' to lose playcalling duties
articles.description: Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb said that "it's not ideal" to have been stripped of playcalling duties, but said he plans to "be the best offensive coordinator I can be."
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコスのOCデイビス・ウェブ、プレーコール権の喪失は「理想的ではない」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスのオフェンシブコーディネーターであるデイビス・ウェブは、プレーコールの権限を剥奪されたことは「理想的ではない」と述べたが、「最高のオフェンシブコーディネーターになれるよう努める」と語った。
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Though he said "it's not ideal'' to have been stripped of playcalling duties, Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb said Friday he's still "all-in'' on quarterback Bo Nix, the team's offense and his role on the coaching staff.

Broncos coach Sean Payton announced Thursday he had made a change and will now call plays instead of Webb. Webb's stint as the playcaller lasted four games as the Broncos' offensive struggled on most fronts in a 2-2 start. The Broncos face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday in SoFi Stadium.

Webb was asked Friday if a four-game sample size was enough to determine a change should be made.

"Luckily that's not my job, that's [Payton's] job,'' Webb said. "I think he answered that. I think the world of him, how we've gone about it ... it's not ideal, but in the same breath, we're 2-2 in the first four games, our first four opponents were a combined 13-3 to start the season. Welcome to the league.''

The Broncos did face four teams currently among the league's top 10 in scoring defense over the first four weeks -- Jacksonville (No. 2), San Francisco (No. 3), Kansas City (No. 6) and the Los Angeles Rams (No. 9). The Chargers are 24th in the league in scoring defense.

"Any time it happens in any aspect of your life job-wise (there's disappointment), but in the same breath that's the NFL, you get going,'' Webb said. "Been a backup QB, been up and down before, that's kind of how it goes.''

Payton had called Webb "a gifted coach'' when he announced early in the offseason his decision to have Webb call plays. Webb interviewed for both head coaching and offensive coordinator jobs elsewhere in the offseason.

And even Thursday, as he announced he would call plays, Payton said Webb is a future head coach in the league.

But throughout the first four weeks of the season Payton has also consistently said he's been frustrated with the team's lack of consistency in the run game as well as their difficulties on first down that has often put the offense in difficult down-and-distance situations.

The Broncos are near the bottom of the league rankings in scoring (27th), total yards per game (27th), rushing yards per game (29th), passing yards per game (20th), QBR (23rd) and Offensive EPA (22nd at -7.48). Only six teams have had more three-and-out possessions than the Broncos this season as 27.5% of their possessions have ended with three downs and a punt.

Nix's play has also been a concern. He is currently 22nd in the league QBR (46.1) and 27th in average air yards per attempt (5.9) as the lack of big plays on offense has become a four-game trend.

The Broncos, overall, are 29th in the league in plays of 20 or more yards and 30th in explosive plays with 16 (runs of at least 10 yards and pass plays of at least 20 yards). Payton said Thursday he hoped the change would repair some issues and those fixes would then help Nix.

Chelsea are keeping an eye on Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong, while Scott McTominay's contract talks at Napoli have stalled, with Real Madrid reportedly interested in making a move. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are monitoring Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong's situation ahead of the January transfer window, reports Spanish outlet Sport. Barça will assess the 29-year-old's playing time as he returns from a knee injury, with increased midfield competition potentially limiting his opportunities. Chelsea remain attentive after sanctioning Enzo Fernández's move to Manchester City, while Barcelona have not ruled out any scenario. However, De Jong remains determined to stay and reclaim a starring role under Hansi Flick.

- Real Madrid have contacted Scott McTominay's representatives amid stalled contract talks with Napoli, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Scotland midfielder could also attract approaches from Premier League clubs if an agreement remains elusive. Napoli may nevertheless block a January departure, keeping their star player for the remainder of the season while allowing themselves more time to negotiate an extension. As a result, any potential transfer is likely to be pushed back until next summer.

- Bayern Munich are monitoring Brighton & Hove Albion center back Luka Vuskovic, German journalist Christian Falk reports. The Croatia international is interested in joining Bayern, but the German champions would first need to offload Kim Min-Jae or Hiroki Ito to create space and funds for another defender. Vušković, who impressed on loan at Hamburg last season, remains on their shortlist, although Bayern are unable to make an offer as it stands.

- Real Madrid forward Endrick is open to joining AC Milan on loan in January, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. The 20-year-old has indicated that Milan would be among his preferred destinations if Madrid sanctions a winter departure, having struggled for playing time this season. AS Roma and Aston Villa are also interested, but Milan could benefit from owner Gerry Cardinale's strong relationship with Endrick's representatives at Roc Nation. Any move remains dependent on Madrid's approval.

- Real Madrid expect Michael Olise to sign a new contract with Bayern, Sky Germany reports. Bayern have held preliminary talks over a contract extension as his current deal runs until 2029, with improved terms potentially making him the club's highest-paid player. A move to Madrid remains a possibility, but Olise is likely to stay if the Spanish giants do not make a concrete approach. Bayern may consider letting him leave the club if renewal talks fail.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick: No timeline for Benjamin Sesko's Man United return
articles.description: Michael Carrick has said there is no timeline for Benjamin Sesko's return after the Manchester United striker suffered a second shin injury.
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック：ベンジャミン・シェシュコのマン・ユナイテッド復帰時期は未定
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのストライカーであるベンジャミン・シェシュコが2度目の脛の負傷を負ったため、復帰の目処は立っていないと述べた。
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has said there is no timeline for Benjamin Sesko's return after the Manchester United striker suffered a second shin injury.

Sesko withdrew from international duty with Slovenia after missing the 1-1 draw with Fulham before the break. Carrick has confirmed the 23-year-old is recovering from a similar problem that kept him out for three months over the summer.

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

- Carrick on City: Medals can't replace 'moments'

- Premier League reranked: Have we found Arsenal's fatal flaw? Why are Chelsea so bad?

Sesko will miss Tottenham's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday and Carrick has acknowledged he doesn't know when he'll be back.

"It's not the exact issue, it's a similar area, but it's not the exact same thing again," Carrick said on Friday.

"We're kind of still working through it a little bit to see how long the issue will be. We're hoping that it'll be soon, obviously, but at this moment it's still not quite clear."

Patrick Dorgu is also sidelined after suffering a hamstring injury playing for Denmark. Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt to face Spurs, but Carlos Baleba could feature for the first time since his summer move from Brighton.

"Patrick came off and looks like he'll be out for probably a number of weeks," Carrick said.

"Nous came off and took a knock. He's not quite right yet, so we'll have to see how he is. Carlos has improved, he's trained a lot.

"Amad's done a little bit of training, Marcus [Rashford] has done a little bit of training, Kobbie [Mainoo] has done a little bit of training. So, a little bit mixed really between the group."

articles.headline: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith among Eagles ruled out vs. Jaguars
articles.description: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley, receiver DeVonta Smith, new starting center Drew Kendall, safety Marcus Epps and receiver Hollywood Brown were all ruled out for Sunday's game in London against the Jaguars.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Running back Saquon Barkley and receiver DeVonta Smith are among the prominent Eagles players who have been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Smith (hamstring) will be sidelined for the second straight game while Barkley (hamstring) will miss his first start of the year after exiting early in the first quarter last week against the Los Angeles Rams.

New starting center Drew Kendall (knee) was not able to practice this week and has been ruled out. He took over center duties in Week 2 for Cam Jurgens, who moved to left guard to account for the absence of Landon Dickerson.

Jurgens, a two-time Pro Bowl selection at the center position, was traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday.

Jake Majors lined up at center during the portion of Wednesday's practice open to reporters.

Safety Marcus Epps (groin) and receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) have also been ruled out. Edge Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is questionable despite not practicing this week.

Greenard left in the third quarter against the Rams and did not return. He missed the first two games of the regular season with a pec injury.

The short-handed offense will get a key player back in tight end Dallas Goedert, who injured his knee Week 2 against the Tennessee Titans. Linebacker Zack Baun has cleared concussion protocol and is expected to play as well.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts appeared on the report Friday with a calf injury but has no designation.

Coach Nick Sirianni confirmed receiver Dontayvion Wicks injured his hamstring during Thursday's practice. He was able to practice in a limited capacity Friday and does not carry an injury designation.

articles.headline: Russell Westbrook wants to carry torch for L.A. Olympics
articles.description: Retired NBA player and Olympic gold medal winner Russell Westbrook said he wants to carry the torch when his native Los Angeles hosts the 2028 Games.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Russell Westbrook won a men's basketball gold medal at the 2012 London Olympics, but the former NBA star has a new goal in retirement: to serve as a torchbearer when the 2028 Summer Olympics come to his hometown of Los Angeles.

"I'm putting this out now: I want to be in the presentation of Los Angeles, as it pertains to carrying the torch during the 2028 Olympics," Westbrook said Friday after being honored by the Los Angeles City Council for his community service work.

Westbrook, who announced his retirement in August after 18 NBA seasons, said that he has "challenged" his Why Not? Foundation employees to expand their philanthropic efforts to help achieve his goal.

"To be able to [carry the torch], you have to be able to position yourself to have your hands in so many different areas," he said. "For me, I'm working religiously impacting so many people, advancing technology, energy, education, health care, mental health and wellness. Every aspect, I want to have my hands in to help any way I can."

Westbrook's Los Angeles ties run deep: He attended Leuzinger High School and UCLA, then played for both the Lakers and Clippers during his decorated NBA career.

Los Angeles city councilwomen Heather Hutt saluted Westbrook as a "humanitarian" for his investments in local schools, athletic facilities and development projects.

"Anything I do from basketball to business is based around L.A.," he said. "I wear L.A. on my sleeve. The way I played, the way I operate, even the way I talk and walk is LA. I'll never change that. ... My legacy will be based on how much I give back to the people of L.A."

The nine-time All-Star and 2017 MVP retired as the NBA's all-time leader in triple-doubles. Westbrook, 37, averaged 15.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 6.7 assists for the Sacramento Kings last season, and his decision to step away caught many by surprise given that he was still a productive player.

Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant said Friday that Westbrook's retirement left him "a little sad."

"I thought Russ still had five or six more years left," Durant said of his longtime teammate on the Oklahoma City Thunder. "He's an athletic body that can still impact the game positively. Congrats to him on an iconic career."

Westbrook, who was known for his all-out energy on the court, has no intention of slowing down in retirement. While he said that his induction into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame will "hopefully happen soon," his primary focus is on his hometown.

"While I was playing, [Los Angeles] was my court," Westbrook said. "Basketball was something I was doing for fun. That was my outlet. Being drafted and being in the NBA was great. But ... being able to have more time, since my retirement, to give back more and be more present, that's more important."

articles.headline: England's Djed Spence ready for long-awaited Inter Milan debut
articles.description: England defender Djed Spence could be handed his long-awaited debut for Inter Milan against Parma on Saturday.
articles.body:
England defender Djed Spence could be handed his long-awaited debut for Inter Milan against Parma on Saturday.

Spence completed a £30 million ($40m) switch from Tottenham Hotspur to the Italian club nearly two months ago but is yet to feature for Nerazzurri.

- As San Siro turns 100, AC Milan and Inter prepare to build a new home

- England's Nations League takeaways: Kane makes history, Tuchel steadies ship

However, speaking ahead of his side's clash against Parma at San Siro, Inter head coach Cristian Chivu said Spence, who has been sidelined since the World Cup, is available to play.

"Djed has been training with us for a week," Chivu said Friday. "He's been following the team's programme since Monday, without restrictions or any other issues, and he's completed five good training sessions.

"We mustn't forget his rehabilitation period and the holiday he had after the World Cup. He's been away from the pitch for two months.

"Now he's available and will be in the squad. We're delighted to have him back. We're finally seeing his smile again and getting to see his qualities."

The Italian champions' winning start to their Serie A defence ended with a 2-2 draw at Roma prior to the international break.

Inter trail leaders Roma on goal difference only, but at the other end of the table, Parma have taken just four points from their opening five contests.

But Chivu insisted: "I think that over the years we've learned not to underestimate our opponents.

"We saw the maturity this team reached in that respect last season. We lost the derbies and some other important games, but we didn't get anything else wrong, and that's why we won the league.

"On paper, matches tell you nothing. They don't reveal the whole truth, and we're well aware of that. We try to turn up on Saturday as the best version of ourselves.

"We have to work hard and give everything to win every game, with the right confidence to go out and earn whatever the day has to offer."

Roma head coach Gian Piero Gasperini said he expects his side to challenge Inter for the crown following their recent draw with the champions.

But when pressed as to whether he expects Roma to be their chief protagonists this season, Chivu replied: "Why don't we talk about the team chasing Roma, Como, Juventus or AC Milan? Why is it always about who can stop Inter?

"We know what we are, but to turn our competitiveness into success, we have to fight. We don't need anyone to remind us that we want to wear the crown.

"We have to fight to earn it. It's far too early to talk about these things. We have 13 points, and there are teams on eleven. It's too soon to talk about who is chasing whom.

"We want to remain competitive and achieve our objectives at the end of the season. That's all we can talk about right now."

articles.headline: Tyrese Haliburton hopes to mend fences with Damian Lillard
articles.description: Tyrese Haliburton said he wishes his relationship with Damian Lillard could be repaired after the Pacers star stole Lillard's Dame Time celebration during the 2023 in-season tournament.
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton said he wishes his relationship with Damian Lillard could be repaired after the Indiana Pacers star stole Lillard's Dame Time celebration during the 2023 in-season tournament.

In the first edition of what is now the NBA Cup, Haliburton hit a key 3-pointer with less than a minute left of the Pacers' semifinal win over Lillard and the Milwaukee Bucks, then looked at his wrist -- a la Lillard's celebration.

Haliburton told "The Zach Lowe Show" in an episode published Thursday that the midseason tournament was key for the Pacers ahead of their run to the 2025 NBA Finals but that he understood how his mockery move damaged his relationship with a player he said he had looked up to for "a majority of my life."

"I think what I do regret more than anything is what me and Dame's relationship has become," Haliburton told Lowe. "Because he was a guy who checked on me a lot early in my career, especially when I got traded [from the Kings to Pacers in 2022]."

Neither Haliburton nor Lillard played last season after suffering torn Achilles during the 2025 playoffs. Both are healthy again entering the 2026-27 season and played in preseason games this week.

Haliburton said he missed a chance to meet with Lillard, who returned to the Trail Blazers in the 2025 offseason after being waived by the Bucks, when he didn't go to Portland following a case of shingles.

"I would love to have a conversation [with Lillard] because I just think it became more than it ever needed to be," Haliburton told Lowe. "Put it on me. I was young, in the moment, I was having fun with it, but it was probably a little much. And whatever happened from there happened."

He added that he hoped they could "at least be cordial again."

A meeting could take place when the Pacers host the Trail Blazers on Dec. 17. Indiana plays at Portland on Feb. 18.

Haliburton also discussed his return to the court, saying he still needed to readjust to the speed of the game.

"That's going to be the biggest adjustment for me, just to kind of like slow down," he said.

articles.headline: Jamal Musiala will 'fight his way back' from injury - Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany
articles.description: Vincent Kompany has backed Bayern Munich playmaker Jamal Musiala to overcome his latest injury setback after he was hurt on international duty with Germany.
articles.body:
Vincent Kompany has backed Bayern Munich playmaker Jamal Musiala to overcome his latest injury setback after he was hurt on international duty with Germany.

Musiala suffered what Bayern say is a "minor" muscle tear while warming up for Germany's Nations League clash against the Netherlands on Sept. 24.

It means the 23-year-old is once again on the sidelines amid a frustrating period, having already missed three of Bayern's seven matches this season.

During pre-season, he suffered two on-field collapses which Kompany said were linked to a change in medication used to treat a neurological condition.

"I can relate to his story of setbacks," Kompany said on Friday. "I've experienced that often in my own career. Coming back from that is a great strength.

"I hope he can enjoy playing football again in the coming years, and I believe he will. Once you learn how to come back from moments like these, you carry that ability with you for the rest of your life.

"That's something Jamal has always shown. In every situation, he knows how to fight his way back and he always comes back. We've seen how happy the team and fans are when he scores a goal. We'll experience those moments again."

Musiala is Bayern's only absentee for Saturday's Bundesliga match against Bavarian rivals Augsburg, when Bayern will be seeking to extend their unbeaten start to the season.

- Harry Kane contract talks with Bayern Munich 'very positive' - sporting director

- Vincent Kompany 'proud' of Man City achievements despite guilty verdict over Premier League breaches

- Harry Kane interest in MLS 'fulfilment of a dream' - commissioner

Kompany's side have won six of their seven games, although a 0-0 draw with Schalke last month has kept them narrowly off the pace at the top of the Bundesliga.

Augsburg have slowed after a strong start to the campaign, having conceded six goals in their last three matches, but Kompany remains wary given they were the only team to beat Bayern in the league last season, 2-1 winners at the Allianz Arena in January.

"It's a very important game," he added. "We lost a Bundesliga match last year, against Augsburg. It's still a derby and it's an away game. Augsburg are known for their compact formation and their ability to be very dangerous on the ball.

"They have a lot of individual quality. They have more than people sometimes realise. They've started the season with momentum. It's still a derby, the fans are looking forward to it, and so are we."

After the long international break, Saturday's match is the first of seven in the space of 20 days, with Tuesday's Champions League trip to Norway to face Viking FK on their artificial pitch coming in quick succession.

"We have the squad for it," Kompany said of the packed schedule. "We want to go into every game with 100% conviction. I'd rather play every three days than have a long break...

articles.descriptionJa: チェルシーのアロンソ監督は、代表監督のトーマス・トゥヘルが疑問を投げかけたことについて、コール・パーマーがイングランド代表としてプレーすることに意欲的であると主張した。
articles.body:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insists Cole Palmer is committed to representing England following question marks raised by national team boss Thomas Tuchel.

Tuchel said Blues forward Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to play international football after he withdrew from his country's squad ahead of Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

The 24-year-old has since trained with his club and been declared fit for Saturday's Premier League clash with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso also expects Reece James, Moisés Caicedo and João Pedro to be available as the Blues bid to bounce back from a thumping 3-0 loss at Brentford three weeks ago.

"He has trained the last week, he has felt better," Alonso said of Palmer, who pulled out of England duty due to reported load management.

"We didn't want to rush because we've had enough time.

"The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, he's feeling OK.

"In the Brentford game, we could see he was struggling. For the next part, we have good feeling with him and that he's feeling better.

"He's committed [to England] but he has to be fully fit to play. And when he's fully fit he will enjoy his minutes. We need him in that moment: the club and the national team."

- Man City 'a disgrace; I would throw them out' - furious Ian Holloway

- Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

Palmer was left out of Tuchel's World Cup squad and has featured just three times since the German took charge of England in January 2025.

Blues captain James missed the recent international window amid another hamstring issue, while striker Pedro sat out the Brentford defeat because of a knee injury, and midfielder Caicedo has played only 14 minutes all season due to a persistent calf problem.

"Yes, he's ready to go," Alonso said of Caicedo.

"We have used the time with Moi to be back fit. He's been training good and he's OK to go."

Asked about James, Palmer and Pedro, the Spaniard continued: "They have been able to train, some of them earlier than others.

"We have used the time, and that was the plan. We knew that against Brentford we were with some players struggling but now they have trained well and they are ready to go.

"For the next block of games until the next international break, we have five Premier League games and hopefully they will be available as long but for tomorrow they will be good."

Former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid boss Alonso began his reign with back-to-back league wins but has taken just one point from the last nine available.

"It's going to take time," he said. "We need to keep improving, keep learning. From each game we are learning things but we need to ensure we don't make the same mistakes again, knowing that each game is really tough."

Hoop Collective: Rockets and Mavs expectations live from Media Day in Macao

Goodwill: Pistons inquired about trades for Durant, Leonard

ESPN reporter Vincent Goodwill wrote Friday about why the Detroit Pistons and big man Jalen Duren -- who engaged in a contract stalemate this offseason before Duren got a five-year, $200 million contract -- needed each other. In that piece, Goodwill dropped a nugget on other players Detroit explored adding since its season ended: 

The Pistons inquired about trading for Kawhi Leonard and Kevin Durant this offseason, according to league sources, and were positioned to offer Austin Reaves a big free agent contract if the Los Angeles Lakers opened the door. None of that materialized.
The Pistons had heard Leonard wasn't interested in coming to Detroit amid the Clippers' cap-circumvention scandal, per league sources, and the Rockets weren't willing to engage on Durant despite the close relationship he shares with Cunningham.
